title: Sweep Terms of the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
Money leaves a Keyturn Host Payout Account on the schedule's own rhythm, whether when a trip completes, daily, weekly on the schedule's day, monthly, or only when the host asks for it, and a sweep after the schedule's cutoff hour falls to the next run rather than going out late.

## Ceilings and the monthly count

One transfer never carries more than the schedule's per-transfer ceiling, so a balance above it is sent in several transfers across successive runs, and no more transfers are made in a calendar month than the schedule allows.

## The state the account must stand in

Money leaves the account only while it is active, or on the final sweep that accompanies its closure, and an account on hold or suspended pays nothing out however large the balance.

| State of the account | Does money leave? |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes, on the schedule's rhythm |
| Closed | Only on the final sweep that accompanies the closure |
| On hold | No, however large the balance |
| Suspended | No, however large the balance |

The state is taken from the account's own record, read against the account's reference number together with the balance free to be paid out, before the transfer is made.

## Fees on the way out

A same-day or card-push transfer carries the schedule's instant fee, taken as its own deduction on the same day; a standard transfer carries no fee at all, and a wire or cheque carries its own flat fee instead.

## The request register

Where a host has asked to be paid, the request is evidenced by the payout request register, which carries the request's own reference number, the host the request belongs to and the sum asked for. That register together with what the host states is the authority for the request, the request is identified by its own reference number, and the position is read before the money moves.

## Clauses no longer in force

Two clauses of these sweep terms have been withdrawn and are no longer in force; neither is applied:

> "A sweep carries the payable balance only, which is the available balance less anything held in reserve, and where that balance is under the schedule's minimum nothing goes out and the money waits for the next run."

> "A host on a schedule that pays on request asks for the money themselves, and only the host can make that request, since it is their money being moved."
